subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy & logging (FinLytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy & logging (FinLytics)

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have a shared record. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- PII and sensitive data occasionally included in prompts (customer name, payment tokens) that must not be stored in cleartext.
- Need for auditable request/response logging for regulators but cannot retain raw PII longer than policy allows.
- Multi-tenant separation and data residency (US-only for now).
- Desire to avoid full model fine-tuning with in-house data — prefer inference-time controls (redaction, on-the-fly obfuscation).

Current stack / constraints:
- Frontend -> backend -> Redwood API (hosted/dedicated options discussed).
- Looking for an option that supports KMS-backed encryption and VPC/private deployment for sensitive flows.
- Primary success criteria:
  * End-to-end retention configurable (default 30 days for customer-facing prompts)
  * Audit logs that are searchable and map request IDs to hashed user IDs (no raw PII in logs)
  * Ability to run an initial 4-week pilot with a safe subset of traffic and automated redaction pipeline

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) I attached a short SOC 2 summary for Redwood and our standard security questionnaire (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf).
2) You to share FinLytics' retention and redaction requirements (you mentioned a short internal doc).
3) Schedule a security deep-dive with your security team + our security SME (I can loop Neha).
4) We will propose a mutual action plan and a pilot configuration (private deployment + KMS + audit logging + redaction).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (PDF)

Proposed times for the security deep-dive (PT): Mon 12/13 10:00–11:00 or Tue 12/14 09:00–10:00. Happy to adjust.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy & logging (FinLytics)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: For our retail customer data we require that raw PII not be stored more than 90 days; for enterprise customers we have a contractual requirement to retain certain audit artifacts for up to 7 years but those artifacts must not contain raw PII (hashed/pseudonymized ok).
- Residency: Pilot traffic must stay in US regions.
- Redaction: We use a combination of client-side redaction and server-side post-processing. If Redwood can support configurable pre-store redaction policies (regex + entity-based) that would be ideal.

I'll attach our internal retention summary so you can align the MAP and questionnaire (finlytics-data-retention-requirements.pdf). Also looping in our security alias (security@finlytics.com) — they may add follow-up questions.

Happy to take Mon 12/13 10:00 PT for the deep dive.

Best,
Alyssa Gomez
Head of Product
FinLytics
alyssa.gomez@finlytics.com

Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Data privacy & logging (FinLytics)

Hi Alyssa and FinLytics security team —

Looping in Neha (cc'd), our security product lead, so she can run the technical deep-dive on 12/13. Neha — quick summary of what FinLytics needs before the call:
- Confirm we can deploy a Private (VPC) instance in US regions with KMS integration.
- Provide example audit log format: request_id, timestamp, model, prompt_hash, response_meta, user_hash (no raw PII).
- Support configurable retention windows per dataset (e.g., 30/90/retain-none) and an on-demand purge API.
- Redaction options: pre-store regex rules, entity-based redaction, and a reversible pseudonymization option (customer asks for pseudonymization for enterprise audits).

I attached our filled security questionnaire and a proposed mutual action plan (redwood-security-questionnaire-filled.xlsx). We'll use the deep-dive to confirm the MAP items and the pilot scope.

Action items (pre-call):
- Alyssa / security@finlytics: share any additional retention clauses or SOC evidence you want us to surface.
- Neha: prepare sample audit log and a short doc on retention/purge APIs.
- Rishi: prepare a rough pilot pricing outline for a 4-week dedicated pilot (private deployment).

See you Monday 12/13 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa

On Fri, 11 Dec 2026 at 09:05 Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finlytics.com> wrote:
> Confirmed for Mon 12/13 10:00 PT.
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Pilot config + ballpark

Quick internal note before Monday's deep-dive:

- Proposal: Private deployment in US (dedicated VPC), KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs shipped to a customer-controlled S3 (with server-side encryption) and an obfuscation layer that stores prompt_hash + user_hash.
- Retention options: default 30 days for pilot (can configure per dataset to 90 days), support on-demand purge and export for audit.
- Redaction: offer regex + entity-detectors at ingress; option to run pseudonymization pipeline before logs hit storage.
- Ballpark for 4-week pilot (engineering + infra + support): $45k–$60k (one-time pilot setup + 4 weeks of reserved capacity) — will refine after scoping.

Neha — if you can bring the sample audit log and retention API notes that should cover the FinLytics asks. I'll draft the MAP doc and share before the call.

-Rishi
